outcome.answer: Yes. One paper reports that five textbook GNNs, including GAT, GINE, GraphSAGE, and R-GCN, trained on one knowledge graph can transfer zero-shot to 40 inductive link-prediction benchmarks on unseen graphs, and the best off-the-shelf GAT matches a dedicated foundation model [1]. Another paper says a GraphSAGE backbone can be used for directed link prediction and outperforms state-of-the-art GDL techniques on several benchmarks, but it does not focus on unknown knowledge graphs specifically [2].
